summary: Retest of iteration_4 nav fixes. Nav overflow and 44px touch-target fixes both VERIFIED across 360/390/412px mobile viewports on /catalog, /catalog/admin, /account. Desktop 1920px nav renders correctly in a single row (height 61px). Backend build2_catalog_gates.py regression: 15/15 PASS. However, /admin route still shows page-level horizontal overflow (scrollWidth=597px) at all three mobile viewports due to the wide Organizations table content (not the nav). Nav CSS changes are fully working; the /admin table is an unrelated pre-existing page-body overflow.

ui_bugs.issue: Page-level horizontal overflow at mobile widths: documentElement.scrollWidth=597 vs viewport 360/390/412. Root cause is the wide Organizations <table> (Ref, Name, Type, Status, Created, Actions columns) which does not shrink or scroll within a container. Nav itself no longer overflows.

issues: Data table forces the whole page to horizontally scroll; wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto container so only the table (not the entire page) scrolls.

action_items: Wrap the Organizations table on /admin (and any other wide tables) in a div with overflow-x:auto and max-width:100% so the mobile page itself does not horizontally scroll. Then re-verify RETEST-1 acceptance on /admin at 360/390/412px.
critical_code_review_comments: index.css .top-nav fix is correct and minimal: flex-wrap + max-width:100vw + min-height:44px inline-flex on links. No regressions on desktop.
Consider adding a shared .table-wrap { overflow-x:auto; max-width:100%; } utility to prevent any wide-table page-overflow across admin views.

Only remaining item is /admin page-body horizontal overflow from Organizations table (scrollWidth=597 at 360/390/412). Backend gates 15/15 green (see build2_gates_retest.xml). rca of the issue: Nav fix: verified. Remaining /admin overflow RCA — the AdminOrganizationsPage renders a raw <table> with 6+ columns of fixed-width text (org refs, names, timestamps). Because no scrollable wrapper exists, the table forces the document to a min width of ~597px, so documentElement.scrollWidth exceeds any mobile viewport. Mitigation: wrap the table in <div style={{overflowX:'auto', maxWidth:'100%'}}> or a .table-wrap CSS class.
